checks.title: GDPR territorial and material scope
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 2-3 and current EDPB territorial-scope guidance. Establish the relevant processing activity, EU/EEA establishment context, offering/monitoring nexus, and exclusions. Do not infer scope solely from IP geolocation.

checks.title: Processing principles and accountability
runtime_tests: Trace representative personal-data fields from collection through storage, use and retention; compare actual behavior with declared purpose, minimisation, accuracy and storage controls.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 5 and 24. Confirm lawfulness/fairness/transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, security and accountability are evidenced rather than asserted.

checks.title: Lawful basis by processing purpose
checks.verify: Review GDPR Article 6 and document the specific lawful basis for each material processing purpose. Do not assume consent is always required or that legitimate interests applies without the necessary assessment.

checks.title: Transparency and privacy information
runtime_tests: Open each material collection flow and verify the relevant privacy information is accessible at the appropriate time and matches the actual purposes, recipients, retention approach, rights and transfer information.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 12-14 against the actual collection context, including direct and indirect collection.

checks.title: Consent validity and withdrawal
runtime_tests: With a clean test state, verify any consent relied upon is freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous; optional choices are not bundled by default; withdrawal is available and subsequent consent-based processing stops.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 4(11), 6, 7 and current EDPB consent guidance. Treat consent as one lawful basis, not a universal default.

checks.title: Special-category and criminal-offence data
runtime_tests: Where special-category or criminal-offence data is processed, trace collection, access restrictions, purpose and downstream use with synthetic data.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 9 and 10 and applicable Member State law. Identify the Article 9 condition or Article 10 legal basis where relevant.

checks.title: Children and information-society services
runtime_tests: Where child users are relevant, test the age/parental-authorisation flow with synthetic accounts and verify child-facing information is understandable.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Article 8 and the applicable Member State age threshold for consent to information-society services; do not assume one EU-wide threshold below 16.

checks.title: Data-subject rights workflow
runtime_tests: Exercise synthetic access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection requests as applicable; verify identity checks, routing, response records and resulting data changes.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 12 and 15-21. Applicability and exceptions differ by right and legal basis.

checks.title: Automated decision-making and profiling
runtime_tests: Where solely automated decisions may produce legal or similarly significant effects, exercise a synthetic case and verify the documented safeguards and human-intervention path where required.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Article 22 and applicable guidance. Do not label ordinary analytics or every AI feature as an Article 22 decision.

checks.title: Controller/processor roles and contracts
runtime_tests: Compare configured vendors/subprocessors and data flows with the processor inventory and contract instructions; verify deletion/return and security obligations where testable.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 24, 26 and 28 plus current EDPB controller/processor guidance. Determine role per processing activity rather than by contract label alone.

checks.title: Records of processing and governance evidence
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 24 and 30, including the Article 30(5) exception and its limits. Check whether processing records and accountability evidence reflect actual operations.

checks.title: Data protection by design and by default
runtime_tests: Inspect default settings and a representative user journey; verify only personal data necessary for each specific purpose is processed by default and access/exposure is appropriately limited.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Article 25 and current EDPB data-protection-by-design/default guidance.

checks.title: Security of processing
runtime_tests: In an isolated environment, test authentication/authorisation boundaries, tenant separation where relevant, recovery, logging, encryption/pseudonymisation controls where appropriate, and processor security dependencies.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Article 32. Required measures are risk-based; Beacon does not prescribe one universal control set.

checks.title: Personal-data breach response
runtime_tests: Run a tabletop or synthetic incident; verify detection, risk assessment, breach register, supervisory-authority decision path and affected-person communication path, including the 72-hour authority-notification rule where applicable.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 33-34 and current EDPB breach-notification guidance. Not every breach requires notification, but controllers must assess and document the decision.

checks.title: Data protection impact assessment
runtime_tests: For a high-risk processing scenario, trace whether the DPIA workflow captures necessity/proportionality, risks to individuals and planned mitigations before deployment.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 35-36, regulator lists and relevant guidance. DPIA applicability is risk- and context-dependent.

checks.title: DPO and EU representative applicability
runtime_tests: Where a DPO or Article 27 representative is required, verify the published contact/representative information is reachable and matches governance records.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Articles 27 and 37-39. DPO and representative duties have different triggers and should not be conflated.

checks.title: International data transfers
runtime_tests: Compare actual storage/processing/support regions and subprocessors with the documented transfer map and selected transfer mechanism.
checks.verify: Review GDPR Chapter V, current adequacy decisions and any relied-on safeguards such as SCCs. A vendor's location alone does not establish whether a restricted transfer occurs or whether safeguards are sufficient.

checks.title: Terminal-equipment storage/access and tracking
runtime_tests: In a clean browser profile, capture storage and network activity before and after user choice; identify cookies/local storage/device-access operations and distinguish strictly necessary operations from consent-dependent tracking.
checks.verify: Review ePrivacy Directive Article 5(3), GDPR consent standards, and the relevant Member State implementation/guidance. The Directive is implemented nationally, so Beacon must not treat one Member State's details as EU-wide.

checks.title: Electronic direct marketing
runtime_tests: Use test recipients to verify the applicable consent/soft-opt-in path, sender identity, unsubscribe mechanism and persistent suppression. Separate email, SMS and other channels where national rules differ.
checks.verify: Review ePrivacy Directive Article 13, GDPR where personal data is processed, and the relevant Member State implementation. National rules and business-recipient treatment can differ.

limitations: This pack is a launch-readiness model, not legal advice or certification.
ePrivacy Directive duties are implemented through Member State law; national requirements must be checked for the markets and establishment involved.
National GDPR derogations, regulator lists and sector-specific laws are not exhaustively modeled.
A PASS reflects the supplied evidence contract for the modeled check, not a legal conclusion.
